title: NATO: what is it still for?
subtitle: 1949 to present
subject: comprendreLeMonde
description: Founded against the USSR in 1949, the **NATO** should have disappeared with the Cold War. Today it is bigger and more active than ever.

hero.hook: Created to confront an enemy that has not existed since 1991, NATO has never had so many members.

blocks.text: **NATO**, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, is the most powerful military alliance in modern history. Founded in 1949 at the height of the Cold War, it was intended to protect Western Europe against the expansion of the Soviet Union.

The disappearance of its opponent in 1991 did not, however, lead to its dissolution. The organization went through thirty years of searching for an identity, before the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022 put an end to all doubts about its usefulness.

sections.title: The genesis: a shield against the Eastern bloc

blocks.text: NATO was officially born on April 4, 1949, when twelve countries signed the **[[North Atlantic Treaty]]** in Washington. This alliance responds to an urgent need for security, while the Red Army occupies Central Europe. Its first secretary general, Lord Ismay, summed up his mission with a famous phrase: “keep the Russians out, the Americans in, and the Germans under control”.
Iceland is the only NATO member country without a standing army. Its contribution is based on radars, coast guards and the reception of allied planes on its soil.

The heart of the treaty is its , which establishes a principle of collective defense: an attack against one member is considered an attack against all. Throughout the Cold War, this automatic solidarity mechanism deterred any Soviet offensive in Europe, as direct conflict had become far too costly to attempt. **[[Section 5]]**

sections.title: Post-Cold War: enlargement and new missions

blocks.text: The fall of the Berlin Wall and the dissolution of the USSR in 1991 plunged NATO into an identity crisis. Without a designated enemy, the alliance seems obsolete. However, it chooses to reinvent itself around two axes. The first is the massive enlargement towards the East: former  countries, such as Poland or Hungary, then the Baltic States in 2004, joined the organization to protect themselves from a possible return of Russian imperialism. **[[Warsaw Pact]]**

The second axis is an operational transformation: NATO begins to intervene outside its territory, for example during the Kosovo war in 1999, then in Afghanistan after 2001. This expansion towards the East fuels strong resentment in Moscow, where Vladimir Putin denounces a provocation and a breaking of promises made at the end of the Cold War.

sections.title: The shock of 2022 and the return to territorial defense

blocks.text: Russia's invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022 abruptly puts an end to the era of doubts. In a few days, NATO returned to its original mission: to defend European territory. The shock pushes Sweden and Finland, long neutral, to request membership: Finland joins the alliance in 2023, Sweden in 2024.

blocks.caption: Since 2022, NATO countries have provided Ukraine with weapons, intelligence and military training.

blocks.text: The alliance, which now has 32 members, is not directly participating in the fighting in Ukraine to avoid a **nuclear escalation**, but it is coordinating unprecedented logistical support. This war also imposed widespread rearmament in Europe, with Germany releasing massive funds to modernize an army that had been neglected for thirty years.
The organization's acronym exists in two inverted forms in its two official languages: NATO in English and NATO in French.

sections.title: NATO faces the challenges of the 21st century

blocks.text: Beyond the classic Russian threat, NATO must adapt to a new grammar of conflicts. She incorporated  and space as new official areas of operation. Computer attacks against critical infrastructures are now considered attacks that can, in certain cases, justify collective assistance. **[[Cyberspace]]**

The organization is also looking towards Asia: the rise of China is encouraging NATO to establish partnerships with Japan, South Korea or Australia, which worries certain European members, who fear a move away from the initial geographical area.
NATO grew from 12 to 32 members between 1949 and 2024. It repositioned itself as the central pillar of European security against Russia, while integrating new areas of conflict such as cyberspace.
